_README: THE WALLS / COMPONENT HEALTH -- the data behind panel 1 of tools/status_gui.py.

IT LIVES IN notes/ AND NOT IN data/ ON PURPOSE: `.gitignore` line 43 is `data/*`, so a copy under data/ would be invisible to git and absent from a fresh clone, and panel 1 would come up MISSING for the next person. It also belongs beside its authority document, notes/PLAN.md.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. notes/PLAN.md section 3 holds the component table, but its cells are
prose, so a GUI cannot pull a SCORE and its FLOOR out of them as a pair. This file is the
structured transcription. It is NOT a second source of truth: every number carries a
`verify` list of literal strings that MUST still be findable in notes/PLAN.md or
notes/STATUS.md. tools/status_state.py checks them on every refresh and renders a row as
CHECK-PLAN when a string has gone missing, so an edit to the plan that moves a number shows
up in the window as a mismatch instead of the window quietly showing a stale figure.
Dash characters are normalised to '-' before comparison, so an en-dash in the plan matches.
THE RULE THIS FILE ENFORCES: a score is NEVER shown without the floor it must beat.
The whole 'we beat scramble' era was a floor error. If a floor is not known, say MISSING.
Do not put a number in `score` unless it was computed off disk and the evidence pointer is
real. MISSING is information; an invented number is damage.
FIELDS
id            stable key
title         plain-language name the owner sees
what_it_does  ONE plain sentence. No jargon. The owner has said twice that jargon makes
our artifacts unusable to them.
instrument    YES | PARTIAL | NO  -- can we measure this part ON ITS OWN?
instrument_note / instrument_evidence
score / score_detail            null score means MISSING (render as MISSING, never 0)
floor / floor_detail / floor_name   the strongest no-understanding baseline on the
IDENTICAL scorer, n, pool and gold
standing      ABOVE_FLOOR | BELOW_FLOOR | LEVEL | UNKNOWN
separated     YES | NO | UNKNOWN  -- are the confidence intervals actually apart?
evidence      where the number came from
verify        literal strings that must still appear in the plan/status docs
_CORRECTION_2026_08_16: THE HEADLINE FLOOR BELOW IS NOT THE STRONGEST FLOOR, AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT OF THIS BLOCK.
The pair `4.80% vs SPELLING 8.70%` stays exactly as it is: both numbers come from the same
cell, the same items, the same pool and the same gold, and that is what makes them comparable.
Substituting the constant guess into the `floor` field would carry a number across scorers,
which is standing discipline 11 and cost this project three retractions in one night.
So the superseding floor is added as its OWN object, `governing_floor`, with its own scope,
and the window renders it ABOVE the table so the 8.70% can never be read without it.
WHY THIS COULD BE FIXED NOW AND NOT BEFORE. The previous agent left the stale headline in
place and explained why: this file's `verify` literals were checked against notes/PLAN.md and
notes/STATUS.md only, the correction exists in neither, and notes/PLAN.md is do-not-touch --
so writing the correction here would have rendered the row CHECK-PLAN. The fix was to ADD
notes/LONG_TERM_PLAN.md to the authority corpus in tools/status_state.py, where the correction
actually lives. Adding an authority document is not editing one, and no do-not-touch file was

governing_floor.title: THE STRONGEST FLOOR WE KNOW OF -- AND IT IS NOT SPELLING
governing_floor.what_it_does: A baseline that gives THE SAME ANSWER TO EVERY QUESTION -- it never looks at what was asked at all.
governing_floor.floor_name: CONSTANT GUESS (uses zero information about the question)
governing_floor.plain_verdict: IT BEATS THE SPELLING CHANNEL, and the spelling channel already beats us. So our score AND the floor quoted throughout the table below are BOTH under a baseline that knows nothing at all. Nobody had ever run this comparison.
governing_floor.detail: It beats spelling by +0.0523 [+0.0391,+0.0658] and +0.0627 [+0.0475,+0.0778], intervals separated.
governing_floor.scope: Measured in a different cell from the 4.80% headline. It is quoted here as the strongest floor we know of, NOT as a like-for-like replacement for the 8.70% -- the two numbers below share a scorer and this one does not.
two_readings: OUR FLOORS WERE TOO WEAK: the standing bar never included a popularity-shaped floor, so it under-set the bar everywhere.

THE TASK MAY BE DEGENERATE: if a constant answer wins, this task may be dominated by which words are common rather than by understanding. These two are distinguishable by measurement, and that measurement is the top priority.
verify: CONSTANT RANKING THAT USES ZERO INFORMATION ABOUT THE QUERY

headline.title: THE WHOLE THING, END TO END: name the right word
headline.what_it_does: Given everything the machine has read, ask it to name the right word out of the whole vocabulary.
headline.instrument_note: Live open-vocabulary read-out, same items, same pool, same gold as the floor.
headline.floor_detail: three-letter chunks of the spelling and nothing else -- zero substrate signal; confidence interval 7.83 to 9.60
headline.floor_superseded_by: This is NOT the strongest floor. A CONSTANT GUESS that never looks at the question beats the spelling channel CI-separated -- see the governing floor above.
headline.plain_verdict: WE LOSE TO A SPELL-CHECKER. A channel that knows nothing but spelling beats us by 1.8x, and the intervals do not overlap. Prefix-only spelling (5.88%) also beats us. AND THE SPELLING CHANNEL IS NOT THE FLOOR THAT GOVERNS: a constant answer that never looks at the question beats spelling too.

components.title: Word and concept encoding
components.what_it_does: Turn a word into a code that is still recognisably that word AND that carries how it relates to other words.
components.instrument_note: 21 of 21 validity gates pass. Measures identity and structure on separate axes, each with its own null arm and its own known-answer arm.
components.score_detail: agreement with human word-similarity judgements; confidence interval -0.006 to 0.216
components.floor_detail: a code carrying no meaning scores zero here
components.plain_verdict: IDENTITY IS FINE. MEANING IS NOT ESTABLISHED: the interval includes zero. Worse, the encoder actually running in production is a scrambled hash of the spelling -- it IS the no-meaning null by construction (meaning-agreement -0.0019). It has no registry row at all.
components.evidence: notes/PLAN.md section 3 row 1 and section 2 items 1-2; hdlab/grounding_acquisition_loop.py::context_vector

components.title: Storage
components.what_it_does: Hold many things at once so that any one of them can be asked for individually and comes back unchanged.
components.instrument_note: NO ISOLATED INSTRUMENT EXISTS. This is the highest-priority item in the plan, not the lowest: you cannot improve what you cannot measure alone. A draft spec exists but its central premise was falsified and must be revised first.
components.floor_detail: will be: CI-separated above the strongest of scramble, spelling and frequency, AND key sensitivity at least 0.15
components.plain_verdict: UNMEASURED. What we do know from reading the running code: the store applies NO KEY AT ALL. Things are added together into one pile. That is not a damaged address, it is an absent one.
components.evidence: notes/PLAN.md section 2 item 5: runtime reconstruction shows acc += symbol_vector(w)

components.title: Reading and extraction
components.what_it_does: Turn a sentence into the facts that the sentence actually states.
components.instrument_note: Scored against independent gold, but not with the full floor battery.
components.floor_detail: NO FLOOR ON RECORD for this component
components.plain_verdict: ROUGHLY 3 OF EVERY 4 FACTS WE STORE ARE WRONG. And this number has no floor beside it, so it cannot currently be graded. A storage instrument must score 'did what went in come back out', never 'is it true', or it will measure this component and report it as storage.
components.evidence: notes/PLAN.md section 3 row 3 and the 3->2 row of section 4

components.title: Retrieval
components.what_it_does: Given a cue, put together a shortlist that contains the right answer.
components.instrument_note: Scored on the identical items, pool and gold as its floor.
components.score_detail: how often the right answer is somewhere in our top 50
components.plain_verdict: FINE, BUT NOT A WIN. We are level with spelling, not above it. Caution: retrieval looking healthy is partly a SYMPTOM of storage having no structure to address -- retrieval compensates by scoring everything.
components.evidence: notes/PLAN.md section 2 'We now know which part fails'

components.title: Selection
components.what_it_does: Out of that shortlist, pick the one right answer.
components.instrument_note: Same items, same pool, same gold as its floor.
components.score_detail: how often we pick the right one out of the shortlist
components.plain_verdict: THIS IS WHERE WE LOSE, AND THE INTERVALS ARE SEPARATED. But do NOT go and improve the selector: it is being asked to sort by meaning using a code that has no meaning in it. Two upstream defects (a meaning-free encoder, a key-free store) both show up here as the same symptom.
components.evidence: notes/PLAN.md section 2, and the 1->5 row of the integration table in section 4

components.title: Foundation (the assembled knowledge base)
components.what_it_does: Of the facts sitting in the finished knowledge base, how many are actually right.
components.instrument_note: First version of this harness whose own validity gates pass: a random decoy scores 0.04 where earlier versions scored it 0.76. Every number the three earlier versions produced was void.
components.plain_verdict: CLEARS ITS FLOOR -- the one component here that does. But this is roughly 49% correct, HALF the 95-97% that three earlier harness versions claimed. Not vindication. A corpus defect is flagged and NOT fixed.

watch_items.title: The learned encoder: not established, NOT refuted
watch_items.detail: Trained here, on our own text, 121,082,196 tokens. Scores 0.189 against a hardened frequency floor of 0.080 -- but the margin's interval runs from -0.026 to +0.241, so it crosses zero. 322 word pairs cannot tell. A bigger run is the plan's item 5. Record: NO_ASSET_CLEARS_THE_HARDENED_FLOOR.

watch_items.title: The one thing that is never allowed
watch_items.detail: Making a number look better by giving the system a shortcut that carries no understanding. Spelling is the live example: a spelling channel already cleared our old '>=10%' gate, which is why that gate was retired. A floor is cleared by understanding, never adopted.
verify: A floor is cleared by understanding, never adopted
